assumptions: Importers can provide lawful shipment-data exports sufficient for an initial diagnostic without a deep systems integration.
The service remains analytical and does not represent itself as an accredited verifier or control the official filing.
The founder caps account scope and does not hire ahead of prepaid evidence of positive contribution economics.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Several paid diagnostics from in-scope importers demonstrating the responsible budget owner, realized price, sales cycle, CAC, delivery and support hours, measured certificate or labor value, and conversion to paid monitoring; signed workflow and data-retention rights; cohort renewal; and evidence of a repeatable acquisition channel.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign identifies the sharper decision: whether the benefit of verified actual values exceeds their collection and assurance cost. This preserves the regulatory cash-exposure trigger while avoiding the false premise that supplier actual data is always indispensable.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Importers face certificate exposure, recurring preparation work, and a consequential default-versus-actual choice; external CBAM solution use is evidenced. Willingness to pay for this separate diagnostic and monitoring offer, its budget owner, and the frequency of economically meaningful decisions remain unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Fixed scope, advance billing, capped support, subscription monitoring, and prepaid specialist add-ons materially improve cash conversion and limit delivery variance. However, proposed pricing, CAC, delivery hours, margins, conversion, renewal, and owner earnings remain entirely unvalidated against a low-priced software benchmark.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: In-scope importers with material certificate exposure form a clearer, economically selected beachhead than generic mid-market importers. The exemption nevertheless leaves fewer, larger accounts with potentially long enterprise sales cycles, and regional account economics are unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: An integration-neutral decision layer that complements brokers, ERPs, and verifiers is more focused than a generic data desk. Yet exposure comparisons are readily bundleable, no customer workflow position is held, and no evidence establishes a segment where the service can dominate.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Importer exposure models and integration mappings could extend across CBAM sectors, jurisdictions, declaration readiness, procurement decisions, and adjacent carbon-cost workflows. The path is credible but depends on lawful reuse of customer-derived mappings and successful adoption in the initial segment.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Embedded importer workflows and accumulated decision benchmarks could create modest switching costs and learning effects. Agreements are unsigned and nonexclusive, customer data reuse may be restricted, and software vendors, brokers, or SAP can reproduce the analytical feature set.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer could be faster and more economical than indiscriminate supplier-data collection by explicitly comparing defaults with actual values and containing service scope. No measured time saving, certificate saving, accuracy advantage, or buyer preference yet proves that this is enough to displace existing workflows.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2026 definitive regime, published certificate prices, and coming annual declaration create an immediate decision window and recurring monitoring need. Incumbent product launches also show demand but compress the window for differentiation.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Founder-controlled targeted outreach improves relationship control, and adviser or association referrals can supplement it without becoming essential. Still, no qualified pipeline, meeting rate, paid conversion, referral agreement, CAC, or repeatable channel exists, and concentrated larger buyers may demand high-touch selling.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A standardized diagnostic fits the founder's data and modeling skills, can start within available capital, and is more compatible with part-time work than open-ended supplier operations. Regulatory liability, enterprise selling, data quality, security, specialist review, and maintenance remain meaningful execution risks.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a distribution-and-data wedge through a repeatable vertical beachhead agreement, ideally with an adviser or importer cluster, that delivers qualified accounts plus permission to retain anonymized mappings and benchmarks while preserving direct importer contracts.
main_structural_strength: The productized importer-side decision workflow removes open-ended supplier dependence from the base offer and aligns fixed scope, advance payment, and recurring monitoring with a real regulatory cash decision.
primary_score_limiter: No evidence yet shows that importers will buy and renew a separate decision layer at attractive fully loaded economics when brokers, inexpensive specialist software, and SAP can bundle similar functionality.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The addressable population is narrowed to fewer larger importers, while CBAMable prices broad workflow functionality at £199-£699 monthly and SAP offers an end-to-end integrated solution, making standalone acquisition and premium pricing difficult.
